exposure: Implementation of a labor and delivery care bundle
cohort: 5826 women who delivered at an academic, tertiary care institution over a 3 year period, before and after the implementation of an intervention to decrease adverse outcomes
finding: The implementation of a labor and delivery care bundle was associated with a decrease in the Modified Weighted Adverse Outcomes Index and Modified Severity Index, particularly among high-risk pregnancies, but not the Modified Adverse Outcomes Index.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate was increasing prior to the intervention, but the rate was stable after the intervention, and the absolute rate did not differ between the pre- and the postintervention periods.
